# `enum-removed`

Enum removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `enum-removed` (both directions), `enum-removed-in-request`, `enum-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An `enum` was removed, so any value of the type is allowed.

## Why this default

In requests: more values are valid. In responses: clients written for the closed set may fail on other values.

## Example

From test case [`enum-removed`](../../test/cases/enum-removed/): A response enum was removed.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           enum:
-           - a
-           - b
```

Findings:

- `enum-removed-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  enum-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the enum in responses if clients rely on it.
